_doc: Canonical symbol map: semantic name -> Ravenswatch engine function/global. This is the source of truth (like Minecraft mappings). Ghidra names, the loader C++ header, and the Python SDK constants are all GENERATED from this file via `rsmm symbols gen`. Resolution: `raw` joins to data/function_patterns.json by name for version-resilient (byte-pattern) lookup; `anchor` is an inlined routine reached as parent_pattern + offset; `va` is a base-relative absolute (data globals, which have no code pattern). `status`: ok = pattern/anchor resolvable in the current corpus; va = base-relative only; unverified = documented in an older corpus, not yet re-confirmed against the shipped pattern DB.

symbols.name: Account_GetDisplayName
symbols.note: Platform display name for an account object, written into `out` as an MSVC std::string (32 bytes, SSO under 16 chars). One function per platform key: it branches over the strings `gamertag` (Xbox), `personaName` (Steam), `pseudo`, and `Nickname`, so it is the engine's single name abstraction. Its only direct caller is FUN_14044a050, the login/session bring-up, which means this is confirmed for the LOCAL account and not yet proven reachable per-peer. Recorded because the ally-name hunt kept re-deriving it: the exe imports EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll (Lobby/P2P/Connect) and NOT steam_api64.dll, and imports no EOS_UserInfo_* at all, so no ally name can come from the platform SDK - remote names must arrive over the game's own session layer. That they exist at all is settled by the shipped text keys Menu_PauseAskerName and Session_Peer_Disconnect. NOT called by the SDK: it takes an out-string the caller owns and an account pointer we cannot yet validate.

symbols.name: Analytics_SubmitNamedEvent
symbols.signature: void(void* analytics_mgr, void* payload_kv, StringDesc* event_name, char has_run_ctx)
symbols.note: CENTRAL TELEMETRY SINK. ~37 gameplay callers funnel named analytics events through here (run_end, enemy_killed, matchmaking_start, level_up_reach, level_up_book, ...), each building a key-value payload then submitting as JSON (projectId 'passtech-ravenswatch') to Passtech's analytics backend over an authenticated HTTP POST. param_3 is a StringDesc { const char* ptr @+0x0; uint32 len|0x80000000 @+0x8 } holding the event name. The loader 'firehose' detour (hook_events.cpp::install_analytics_firehose) reads that name and re-publishes it to the Lua bus by its raw name, so ONE hook exposes every named event to mods (R.on('enemy_killed', cb)) and survives the game adding new event names. OBSERVATION-GRADE: these fire AFTER the gameplay action and carry analytics KV, not live entity handles — good for 'when X happens do Y' triggers, not for mutating the actor. For entity-context gameplay events (damage, give-item) see the oCGameNamedEvent bus — mapped: NamedEvent_Dispatch is the single hook point (R.on('gameplay:<NAME>'), docs/_re/kinds/events-bus.md). Skips 'run_end' to avoid double-firing the typed Event_RunEnd table hook. [2026-07-10: recovered via anchor/decompile-verify (batch 2) after the July-9 remap mis-placed it.]

symbols.name: BinarySaver_CollectDependencies
symbols.note: The pre-pass that makes Object_SaveToFile self-contained, NOT a gate (it is the `if (FUN_1404fc950() == 1)` at the head of BinarySaver_WriteGraph). It builds an `oCDependencyParser` — another oISerializer implementation — over the saver's own class table (saver+0x18 +0x6d0/+0x6d8) and object list (+0x6e0/+0x6e8), then calls rootObject->vtbl[3](rootObject, parser) = Serialize. Walking the graph through a fake serializer is how the file's class directory and sub-object list get populated: the caller supplies ONE root object and the engine discovers the rest, versions included. It then drains the collected list, serializing each into the parser, and returns false if any object's Serialize fails.

symbols.name: BinarySaver_WriteGraph
symbols.signature: bool(void* saver, void* rootObject, const char* label, void* ctx)
symbols.note: oCBinarySaver vtable slot 5 (the loader's slot 5 is FUN_140500d70, the reader). Writes the whole cooked file body: `uClassCount`, then per class {rInfo.m_sName, m_uId, m_uVersionMaj, m_uVersionMin, m_uParentId} (0x20 bytes/record, table at saver+0x18 +0x6d0/+0x6d8), then `uOjbectsCount` (engine's typo), then per object its class-table index as `uFoundIndex`, then each sub-object as `SingleObject%d`, then the root. This is byte-for-byte the header rsmm.engine.cooked.parse reads back, INCLUDING the per-class version fields Serializer_GetClassVersion gates optional fields on.

symbols.name: BinarySaver_WriteObject
symbols.signature: bool(void* saver, void* object, const char* label, bool flag)
symbols.note: Writes ONE object through a serializer: calls object->vtbl[1]() = GetClassId, finds that id in the saver's class table, writes the index as `uFoundIndex`, then calls object->vtbl[3](object, saver) = Serialize. PROOF that Serialize is direction-agnostic: slot 3 is the same slot the codec work calls 'Deserialize' (e.g. GameModeDefaultDefinition::Deserialize = vftable slot 3). A def's Serialize branches on serializer vtable slot 4 = IsSaving (oCBinaryLoader returns 0, oCBinarySaver returns 1) -- Definition_DeserializeBase does exactly this at its head -- and transfers fields via the typed slots 13-19 (widths 1/4/8), which read from the loader's stream at +0x68 or write to the saver's at +0x40. So every hand-written Serialize in the engine can WRITE the payloads rsmm's Python codecs still carry as opaque _tail_hex.

symbols.name: DefinitionRegistry_Ctrl
symbols.note: Instance registry SwissTable (absl flat_hash_map) keyed on the class-descriptor pointer; this is the table Registry_EnumInstances find-or-inserts into and Registry_RegisterInstance appends live definitions to. Slot stride 0x18: {u64 key = class desc ptr, u64 data = void** instance array, u32 count @+0x10}. Control bytes are absl's: a byte with the high bit CLEAR marks a full slot (h2 = hash & 0x7f), 0x80 = empty, 0xfe = deleted. THIS entry is the pointer to the control-byte array. Read the table directly instead of calling Registry_EnumInstances when you only want to LOOK: that function is find-or-INSERT, so a miss mutates the map and can trigger a rehash (FUN_140244620) — an allocation on the game's heap from a read-only probe. R.defs walks these three globals with page-guarded reads and never calls in.

symbols.name: Entity_GetNetComponent
symbols.note: SwissTable/F14 component-map lookup on an entity for the fixed type-id 0x154fce5c (the net/replication component). Probes the entity's component map (control bytes @entity+0x5e8, slots @entity+0x5f0, bucket mask @entity+0x600) and returns the component pointer, or 0 if the entity has none (e.g. single-player / non-replicated). The returned component's byte @+0x130 is the local/remote AUTHORITY flag: 0 = locally controlled (this client owns the entity and emits its NETWORK_DAMAGE), nonzero = remotely controlled (apply received state, don't emit). Both hit paths (NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit, the attack resolver FUN_1403dc780) gate network emit on this flag. NOTE: it dereferences the component map unconditionally, so only call on a known-valid entity. Pattern is multi-match (index 3/6, 128-byte sig) — fn_verify-guarded. Relevant to local-vs-remote hero disambiguation in co-op, though hero-capture already pins the local player via the HUD-mirror requirement (only the local player has one). [2026-07-10: recovered via live-Ghidra decompile-verified anchor/call-graph after the July-9 remap mis-placed it mid-instruction.] SLOT LAYOUT (recovered 2026-08-17 from the decompile): the slot array at entity+0x5f0 has stride 0x10 -- {u32 class id @+0, component* @+8} -- and the value at +0x600 is the bucket MASK (capacity-1). That makes the map walkable LINEARLY with page-guarded reads and no hash function, which is how R.damage classifies a damage victim (enemy = carries class id 0x1561073c). The id space is mined by tools/mine_class_ids.py; 0x154fce5c resolving to oCEntityCpntNetwork is that miner's acceptance test. NO FIXED COMPONENT SLOTS: because the map is a hash table, an entity component is NOT reachable at any constant offset from the entity, so a chain of the form `entity+CONST -> +CONST` can never be a structural path to a component (or to anything a component owns). Checked 2026-08-20 after the damage meter briefly seeded two such chains from session 7068 (`entity+0x678 -> +0x2d0`, `entity+0xad8 -> +0x1c0`) as if they were build constants: a sweep of all 65,347 .pdata functions finds ZERO sites loading [X+0x678] then reading [+0x2d0], zero for [X+0xad8] -> [+0x1c0], and +0xad8 is never touched on any register that also walks an entity (the same sweep does find real chains such as [X+0xb8] -> [+0x20], so it is not blind). The only qword-pointer write at +0x678 in entity-shaped code is oe::dt::EntityCpntRecapBookPageSettings::~dtor (FUN_140419aa0), an unrelated UI class. Both chains were heap coincidence; they are no longer seeded, and a chain is only used once observed on the live board. Do not re-derive per-player identity as a constant entity offset.

symbols.signature: void*(void* componentStore, void** out, oCEntity* entity)
symbols.note: Read-only F14/SwissTable lookup that maps an entity to its owned magical-object component. symbols.note: Parses one lobby member's ATTRIBUTE BLOB. param_2 is a StringDesc { const char* ptr @+0x0; uint32 len|0x80000000 @+0x8 } holding the serialized attribute text; the body builds a std::string from (ptr, len) and then matches the attribute keys, which is where the only .rdata copies of "PlayerName" (0x140f14230), "RequestedHero" (0x140fac898), "RequestedSkin" (0x140fac8a8), "InLobby" (0x140fac8b8) and "LobbyState" (0x140fac8c0) are referenced. 12 call sites. HOW IT WAS FOUND (2026-08-16): a linear capstone sweep of .text reports ZERO xrefs to "PlayerName" because it desyncs on inter-function padding - disassembling per .pdata function range resyncs and yields the three real lea sites. WHY IT MATTERS: player display names cannot come from the platform SDK (the exe imports EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll and no EOS_UserInfo_*; Steam can name only the local account), so a remote name reaches this machine ONLY as a lobby attribute. Detouring this is how R.lobby learns names without sweeping the address space: the 32-byte key/value blocks the old scan searched for are this parse's TRANSIENT storage, not a persistent roster, which is why a 4-player session scanned back only 2 members.

Mined 2026-08-21 with Ghidra. ⚠ BASE IS 0x14143f600, NOT 0x14143f650. Netcode_PeerStateTick's `lea rax,[rip+...]` lands on 0x14143f650 because it indexes slot+0x50 (the tunnel pointer) directly; reading the array from there is off by 0x50 and every field comes back from the NEXT slot. The true base is what the slot ctor FUN_1402aedf0 zeroes field by field. Stride 0x60 is fixed by `lea rax,[rax+rax*2]; shl rax,5`. SLOT LAYOUT (FUN_1402aedf0 fills it, FUN_1402b5db0 frees it): +0x00 PlayerName, +0x10 the lobby member's own +0x00 session-id string, +0x20 m_sEosUserId (the engine calls it the "P2P User"), +0x30 uint64 hash of the EOS id (FUN_1402aed50), +0x48 connection handle carrying the SystemAddress, +0x50 the P2P tunnel (+0xc0 uint16 UDP port — FUN_1402aa470 passes it through Ordinal_15 = ntohs, so it is a PORT and NOT a RakNet system index; +0xcc conn-state enum, 3 = connected, 2 = eInterrupted; +0xd0 a timestamp). The three string members are the engine's {void* ptr @+0x0; int32 len @+0x8; uint32 cap @+0xc} descriptor, the same shape LobbyAttributes_Parse's StringDesc uses. HOW THE FIELDS WERE PROVEN: FUN_1402aedf0 calls FUN_140918b00(session_mgr, param_1, &record), which walks the lobby members (0x70 stride), memcmp's each member's +0x00 string against param_1, and on a match runs LobbyAttributes_Parse(&record, member+0x28) — so param_1, stored at slot+0x10, IS the member session id, and the record fields copied out to slot+0x00 and slot+0x20 are record+0x00 (PlayerName) and record+0xa8 (m_sEosUserId) by their stack offsets. FUN_1402b0230 finds the LOCAL slot by comparing slot+0x10 to the global at 0x141300958; FUN_1402b0170 finds a slot by slot+0x20. FUN_140272700 is the engine's own member->slot join: it hashes each parsed member's EOS id and compares against slot+0x30, logging "No tunnel found for P2P User: {}" / "No party member found for P2P User: {}" with slot+0x20 as the argument. WHY IT WAS MINED: the damage board knows every player NAME and a distinct per-row owner RakNetGUID (Entity_GetNetId's note) and nothing joined the two. This table supplies the name directly; the open half is which slot owns which hero row, and slot+0x30 is the engine's own ownership key, so rsmm.lua's F._dmg_peer_join scans each row's controller and entity for it. UNPROVEN in-game. ⚠ va, so build-specific: gate every read on va_globals_trusted. [IN-GAME 2026-08-21, session a34f] The layout READS BACK CORRECTLY on live data: `peer table: 2 peer(s) [#0 fruktik_kiwi eos=0002742cd3f241e6821afcd414945c85 port=59550 state=3, #1 EvilMurray eos=0002b4fab7154a739ef4154809c7f6ea port=33421 state=3]` — real personas at +0x00, real ProductUserIds at +0x20, live ports and state=3 through the tunnel at +0x50, and the peer count equalled the number of remote machines. So this IS a working name table for remote players. ⚠ TWO NEGATIVES from the same session. (1) slot+0x30 is NOT a hash value: it reads 0x2a114260 / 0x2bfbe3a0, i.e. heap addresses in the game's own allocation range, so FUN_1402aed50 returns a POINTER (probably to the interned id) and comparing it across processes is meaningless. (2) Nothing on the hero side carries it: scanning 0x800 of every row's controller and entity gave `hash hits [none]`, and the netcomp locator sweep found +0x2d0/+0x2e8/+0x300 pointing at the SAME player's id on EVERY row — a shared object, not a per-player field. The hero->peer link is therefore NOT on the hero object. The only per-row distinct value remains RakNet::Replica3::creatingSystemGUID, so the next candidate is GUID -> SystemAddress -> the tunnel's +0xc0 PORT, which this table already exposes.

gameplay_event_catalog_doc: Names dispatched on the oCGameNamedEvent bus, mined from the shipped exe by tools/mine_event_names.py (SCREAMING_CASE literal pools in .rdata, kept only where a pool contains an event name independently CONFIRMED in-game). Subscribe with R.on('gameplay:<NAME>', cb). event_payload_schemas_doc: Payload layouts for the oCGameNamedEvent subclasses that carry data, recovered by tools/mine_event_payloads.py (RTTI type descriptor -> complete object locator -> vftable -> the code that stores it, walked within .pdata function bounds). Keyed by VFTABLE RVA, not event name: the loader reads *(ev+0) and matches it exactly, so no name mapping can go wrong. Field OFFSETS and WIDTHS are recovered; field MEANING is not, so names are mechanical (u50 = u32 at +0x50) except where hand-RE confirmed one. Only ~24 of the ~150 event names have a payload at all -- the rest are dispatched as the bare base class (header only). RVAs are build-specific: the loader gates this decode on the build fingerprint (va_globals_trusted) and re-verifies with --verify after a patch.
